evidence: Exact firmware IDB: SAR open allocates a 16-byte list node and 224-byte connection; RX callback is connection+12, not list-node+12.
Encrypted receive uses crypto(session, 0, len, input, output); nonzero return must not dispatch a command.
Transport send encrypts payload in place, then SAR submit copies into an owned queue allocation before returning. Band 11 .179 sub_C98CA30 confirms the synchronous copy.
An LVGL bootstrap initializes a resident libuv timer on the same UI owner loop; Bluetooth RX only decrypts/enqueues. The exact .179 native timer layout is 88 bytes, not .043's 136 bytes.
constraints: Normal builds automatically include this exact target's L2 backend. No extra enable flag is required; generated veneer and symbol approval states are unchanged.
SRAM callback replacement only; Cortex-M33 Flash patching is not used.
Only encrypted requests on 0x43 are accepted. No physical-device validation.

The owner-source replacement is experimental and remains PENDING. UI/LVGL must run once to bootstrap it; do not use forbidden thread/work-queue symbols as a workaround. No physical-device or production approval.

owner_source.context: Owner-only list/heap mutation. The LVGL bootstrap initializes the UI timer on *0x200C3050; encrypted RX initializes the response timer on the Bluetooth loop *0x200D9430. UI dispatches Supervisor commands and queues replies; Bluetooth drains replies and calls transport send within its own task-group fd table. No threads/work queues and no symbol promotion.
